title: Product 02 post-fix independent PDF review
source: Five actual Product 02 PDFs regenerated from the remote-confirmed source SHA using issueReport(); all 35 current PDF answer blocks were read.
method: Manual application of the fixed six-part rubric to extracted text from each actual PDF. Each profile mean is the arithmetic mean of seven answer totals rounded to one decimal. Automated diagnostics were excluded. Current Q3/Q4 changed text was rescored from these PDFs; unchanged answer text retains the prior manual component scores.

answerRecords.questionTitle: Which careers suit me best?
answerRecords.answerFromPdf: Your Answer: Business development, sales or account growth matches your chart's emphasis on finding customers and openings. What This Means for You: A role with room to build relationships and act on an opportunity fits you. A system that adds sales targets without control over delivery creates a sharper mismatch. Bottom Line: Customer growth fits best when delivery stays within your control.
answerRecords.deductionReason: Strong direct role fit and useful job-condition detail; the examples are still role families rather than a tailored occupation, and some practical wording is shared with later answers.

answerRecords.questionTitle: Am I better suited to employment or independent work?
answerRecords.answerFromPdf: Your Answer: Structured employment is better supported by the chart. What This Means for You: For a structured job, your chart shows training or specialist support. For independent work, a customer-income marker appears, but the chart does not show a complete link from useful work to paid customers.
answerRecords.deductionReason: The employment-versus-independent conclusion is clear and chart-supported, but the explanation repeats the same job-setting evidence and does not compare actual pay or work conditions.

answerRecords.questionTitle: How do I naturally make money?
answerRecords.answerFromPdf: Your Answer: Your income pattern has two routes: regular pay or repeat work, and additional income from projects or new customers. Both appear in your chart, rather than a single fixed earning style. What This Means for You: Customer or project income is linked to day-to-day work and shared commitments. Steady pay is linked to your wider network and day-to-day work. These are possible earning routes, not expected pay. Bottom Line: Your chart supports a dependable base plus a second route through projects or customers.
answerRecords.deductionReason: The text accurately states the money route and limits. Where the chart only has a limited, hidden sign, it names a possible route but gives little usable explanation of how that route relates to the customer’s work pattern.

answerRecords.questionTitle: What tends to block my financial progress?
answerRecords.answerFromPdf: Your Answer: A possible pressure is the time or cost of training and support needed for income-related work. The chart cannot show whether this is affecting your actual finances. What This Means for You: The chart points to a possible squeeze between paid work and the preparation or help needed to do it well; it cannot establish the cause of a real setback. Bottom Line: A possible work/support cost pressure appears, but the chart cannot confirm it is a real financial blocker.
answerRecords.deductionReason: The revised lead distinguishes a possible chart pressure from a verified cause. The explanation and bottom line still repeat that distinction and need a more useful chart basis.

answerRecords.questionTitle: When might my career or money situation improve?
answerRecords.answerFromPdf: Your Answer: The calculations do not identify a year when career or financial progress is likely to improve. What This Means for You: The checked years include defined responsibilities and demanding assignments, but none stands out as a clear period of extra support.
answerRecords.deductionReason: It honestly says no clear improvement period is found, but the follow-up is broad and overlaps with the decade outlook rather than offering a distinct answer about timing.

answerRecords.questionTitle: What do the next ten years suggest for my work and money?
answerRecords.answerFromPdf: Your Answer: Your 2026-2035 outlook is mixed: work themes change, but the comparisons do not show a steady rise in income. The main themes include defined responsibilities, demanding assignments, and training and guidance. Important Timing: Work may feel more demanding in 2026, 2029, 2031, 2032. Treat these as review points, not predicted setbacks.
answerRecords.deductionReason: Clear decade-level answer, chart themes and profile-specific years. Minor deduction for dense lists and similar framing across profiles.

answerRecords.questionTitle: What is my most important career and money insight?
answerRecords.answerFromPdf: Your Answer: Your chart places signs for steady pay and income from customers or projects in the same birth-month area that points to customer growth and business development.
